meta.intro: Today's throughline: the binding constraint on AI is moving from chips and models to power, customers and trust, while open Chinese weights and efficiency labs reprice the frontier.
meta.briefingTitle: Kimi K3.1 Closes on Opus 5.5, Flapping Airplanes Raises $1B Pre-Product, and Rapidus Still Has No Customer
meta.summary: The constraint is shifting from supply to demand and delivery. Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro nearly matches Anthropic's best on a third-party index with open weights promised, while a pre-product lab raises $1B on the idea of needing less compute. Meanwhile grid delays cost Nscale its Microsoft site, and in Japan Rapidus gets another ¥400B of state equity but still names no 2nm buyer. Japan's openings are in software and ecosystem layers: agents, connectors, and design services.

gaps.label: Sovereign frontier-model pretraining
gaps.note: Unchanged — Sakana moves up-stack into enterprise agents (Aquarium) while Kimi K3.1 shows open frontier-class weights arriving from China, not Japan.

gaps.label: Depth of private risk capital for AI infrastructure
gaps.note: Unchanged — a $1B pre-product raise in SF and a Sequoia-led $66M Series C in a day; TOKIUM's IPO prices at about ¥16.8B.

gaps.label: Domestic leading-edge chip manufacturing
gaps.note: Up 1 — METI approved TSMC Kumamoto 3nm and signalled ¥400B more for Rapidus, but Rapidus still has no named 2nm customer.

gaps.label: Early-stage AI venture formation
gaps.note: Unchanged — Meta's Muse lands in Japan first outside North America with local connectors, a gap domestic agent startups have not filled.

items.headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro Lands Within Three Points of Claude Opus 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis Index, With Open Weights Promised for Nov 4
items.dek: Moonshot's 2.8T-parameter model costs $2/$10 per million tokens, and its hacking skills were deliberately weakened before release.

analysis.happening: Moonshot released Kimi K3.1 Pro on Oct 23: 2.8T parameters, 104B active, 1M context. Reports put it at 55 on the Artificial Analysis index, up 11 points on K3, behind Opus 5.5 (58) and Sonnet 5.5 (56).
analysis.now: If weights ship as promised, it becomes the top open-weight model, a self-hosting option and a pricing lever on closed APIs. Caveat: scores are third-party tracker figures, and the paid-influencer allegations are unresolved.
analysis.future: Watch whether weights appear by Nov 4, under what licence, and whether Japanese enterprises start evaluating Chinese open weights.

items.headline: Flapping Airplanes, a One-Year-Old Pre-Product Lab, Raises $1B at $6B From Index and Lux to Train Models on Less Data and Compute
items.dek: Top-tier money is now pricing an efficiency research thesis, quadrupling the lab's valuation since a January seed.

analysis.happening: Index Ventures and Lux Capital led $1B at a reported $6B valuation; Sequoia, GV, Kleiner Perkins and Nvidia joined. January's $180M seed implied about $1.5B. The lab has no product, revenue or published results.
analysis.now: Efficiency per chip and per data point is the funded gap, not another chatbot. Caveat: figures are Bloomberg-relayed, and one outlet's 'Series A' label appears nowhere else.
analysis.future: Watch for first technical results or a paper, any Nvidia commercial tie-up, and rival efficiency labs closing at similar marks.

items.headline: Blacksmith Doubles to a $1B Valuation in Two Months on a Sequoia-Led $66M Series C, Selling Faster CI for AI-Written Code
items.dek: As AI writes more code, validating it becomes the bottleneck, and investors are paying up for the plumbing.

analysis.happening: Sequoia led $66M at $1B, up from $550M about two months ago; Premji joined, GV and YC remain. Company-reported: CI jobs rose from 5M to 90M+ per week since January, ARR up 17x to 'tens of millions'.
analysis.now: Picks-and-shovels behind Cursor, Codex and Claude Code: build and test load scales with generated code. Caveat: all traction figures are company-supplied and GitHub Actions competes directly.
analysis.future: Watch GitHub and CircleCI pricing responses, and seed-stage test generation, review and sandboxing startups in the same gap.

items.headline: Microsoft Reportedly Walks From Nscale's UK Site Because Grid Power Slips to the 2030s, Days Before Nscale's US IPO
items.dek: A 50 MW anchor-tenant exit shows grid queue time, not GPU supply, can break a neocloud's story.

analysis.happening: The Telegraph reports Microsoft exited Nscale's Essex campus (50 MW, expandable to 90 MW). UK Power Networks reportedly said power would arrive in the early-to-mid 2030s, not end-2026. Nscale's filing cites a $103.4B backlog, with Microsoft and Anthropic ~85% of contracts.
analysis.now: Backlog is only as good as the grid connections behind it, and concentration magnifies one lost site. Caveat: Microsoft gave no reason, and Nscale says other contracts are unaffected.
analysis.future: Watch Nscale's IPO pricing as a read on the neocloud funding window. Fast-power developers have an opening, in the UK and in Japan's queues alike.

items.headline: Omnara, a Self-Hostable Apache-2.0 Clone of Claude Managed Agents, Hits About 3.3k GitHub Stars Days After a Show HN
items.dek: Agent state lives in your own Postgres event log and runs on any model, so 'managed agents' becomes something a solo builder can host rather than rent.

analysis.happening: Omnara's Show HN reached about 110 points. The repo has roughly 3.3k stars under Apache 2.0: an API, stateless workers, an outbound-only machine daemon and a Postgres event log. It supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock and Ollama, plus Slack, GitHub and cron.
analysis.now: Host and customise your own agent runtime; Bedrock support suits an AWS-fluent builder. Caveats: the README calls local defaults 'intentionally insecure', and the parity claim is the author's own.
analysis.future: Watch for a first tagged release, a hosted-Omnara business, and any lab response on pricing or portability.

items.headline: Japan Plans Another ¥400B Equity Injection for Rapidus (FY2027-29) as It Signs 17 Design Partners but Still Names No 2nm Customer
items.dek: The state is now Rapidus's anchor investor and sales-support function, while the order book is still empty.

analysis.happening: METI signalled a further ~¥400B (~$2.5B) for FY2027-29 to reach 2nm mass production in 2H FY2027. On Oct 7 Rapidus signed 17 design partners, including Synopsys, Cadence, DNP and Toppan. Chairman Higashi says it is 'broadly on track'.
analysis.now: Gap: TSMC already ships 2nm-class volume and Japan has no named Rapidus buyer. Caveat: the ¥400B is a budget request and lender loan intents (~¥2T) are non-binding. Opening: design-service and IP work around the 17-firm ecosystem.
analysis.future: Watch for the first named customer, the December budget, and signed bank loans. A customer-less 2H27 start is the real risk.

items.headline: Sakana AI Launches 'Aquarium', an Ontology-Based Enterprise Agent Platform, Days Before a Tokyo World-Models Symposium
items.dek: Japan's best-funded lab is moving from models into a Palantir-style layer for regulated firms, with no named customers yet.

analysis.happening: Sakana announced Aquarium on Oct 23: an ontology layer linking data without moving it, plus governance (access rights, pre-execution approvals, audit trail) and managed agents with human sign-off. Prior finance projects include MUFG, SMBC and Daiwa. A Tokyo symposium with Schmidhuber follows Oct 26.
analysis.now: Gap: the US has Palantir AIP and lab agent stacks; Japan has no domestic equivalent at scale, and regulated banks may prefer a local vendor. Caveat: no pricing, date or customers, and the Palantir comparison is our read.
analysis.future: Watch for the first named customer and whether the bank projects move onto Aquarium.

items.headline: Meta Brings Its Muse Personal Agent to Japan, First Outside North America, With Mercari, Money Forward ME and Ticket Pia Hooks
items.dek: A US frontier agent lands in Japan about six weeks after its US launch, wired into local consumer apps from day one.

analysis.happening: Meta launched Muse in Japan on Oct 23 on iOS, Android and web, six weeks after its Sept 8 US debut. It sends email, books travel and fills forms, asking approval before sending or buying. Basic features are free; paid pricing is undisclosed.
analysis.now: The time gap is small; the ecosystem gap is large: Japan has no domestic consumer agent of comparable reach, and local connectors are the moat. Caveat: voice and avatar features are not yet available in Japan.
analysis.future: Opening: agent-ready APIs for Japanese services (convenience stores, rail, municipal forms). Watch LINE and Rakuten responses.

items.headline: Accounting-Agent Startup TOKIUM Is Approved for a TSE Growth IPO on Nov 25 at a Roughly ¥16.8B Expected Market Cap
items.dek: One of Japan's few listed 'AI agent' plays is tiny by US standards and still leans on human operators.

analysis.happening: TOKIUM (664A) won listing approval on Oct 16 and lists Nov 25. Indicative price ¥1,620 implies about ¥16.84B market cap. Revenue for the year to May 2026 was ¥5.97B (+29.7%), back to operating profit. Holders include Nissay Capital, Jafco and JIC.
analysis.now: Gap: roughly $110M of value for an end-to-end accounting agent, a fraction of US agent valuations, blended with human operators. Caveat: the price is indicative and bookbuilding (Nov 9-13) could move it.
analysis.future: Watch Nov 16 pricing and first-day trading as a read on appetite for Japanese AI listings. Pitch angle: tax, payroll and procurement with the same agent-plus-human model.
